Proven-equivalent mutant; equivalence argument recorded at the site. `rawFile` is `match[1]`, the DIAGNOSTIC regex's first capture group, which is mandatory (`(.+)`, not optional and not behind an alternation) -- whenever `match` is non-null, `rawFile` is already guaranteed to be a defined string, so `rawFile !== undefined` can never be false when this clause is reached. The `&&` chain was reordered (`path.isAbsolute(rawFile ?? '')` now leads, using `?? ''`, itself killed), Ignored 6->8 (the one targeted mutant plus one new globally-excluded StringLiteral from the added `''`), Survived 1->0. No collateral.

Proven-equivalent mutant; equivalence argument recorded at the site. `.rule?.severity` only runs once `.rule?.name` (the clause immediately above it in the same `&&` chain) has already evaluated true, which requires `rule` to already be a real object -- a nullish `rule` makes `rule?.name` evaluate to `undefined`, never `=== 'string'`, short-circuiting before `.rule?.severity` is reached. So by the time this clause runs, `rule` is guaranteed non-nullish and property access on it can never throw, `?.` or not. Contrast `.rule?.name` itself: nothing gates that access, so `rule` can still be undefined there, which is why the analogous mutant on `.rule?.name` is real, not equivalent (covered by the "no rule object at all" test, not by any suppression). See the ConditionalExpression entry above for this file's before/after counts (all four directives measured together).
